info.name: BusinessSAAS
info.description:
Full Postman collection regenerated from the actual r11 backend source (routes.go + model.go + handler.go across every module, cross-checked against cmd/server/main.go's route registration) on 2026-07-16. Supersedes the previously uploaded collection, which predated HRM, Capture, CRM Templates/Settings/Agenda entirely.

RUN ORDER: 00 Setup -> 01/02 Auth -> 03 User -> 04 Organizations (Create + Switch, which refreshes access_token with business_id set) -> everything else in folder-number order, since later folders assume IDs captured by earlier ones (org_id, contact_id, lead_id, pipeline_id, hrm_employee_id, etc. are auto-saved into collection variables by each Create request's test script).

IMPORTANT — read before importing:

1. Several HRM setup-module and Capture-module list/create endpoints are registered WITH A TRAILING SLASH due to a real StrictRouting quirk in the backend (Group("/") vs Group("") in Fiber v3) — this is NOT a typo in this collection. Affected requests are called out individually in their description field. This was found while building this collection and is not yet in the r11 doc's known-issues list.
    
2. Two requests (CRM / Deals → Get Deals by Contact / by Company) point at handler methods that exist in source but are never wired into routes.go — they will 404 until registered.
    
3. Capture module: only POST /pub/leads is confirmed working end-to-end per the r11 audit. The email/social webhooks ship with zero signature verification (Fix Pass B) — do not point real providers at them. See each request's description for specifics.
    
4. CRM Reports includes two working endpoints (Rep Performance, Forecast) and Companies includes an Enrich endpoint that are not reflected in the r11 master doc's route lists — flagged individually.

request.description: Creates a new user account. Also registered as an alias at POST /auth/sign-up.
Sets the httpOnly refresh cookie (bsaas_refresh) and returns { access_token, expires_in } in the body only — no user object. Also aliased as POST /auth/sign-in.

Reads the bsaas_refresh httpOnly cookie (Postman's cookie jar handles this automatically after Login). Rotates the refresh cookie and returns a new access_token. Also aliased as POST /auth/refresh-token.

Always returns 200 regardless of whether the email exists (prevents enumeration). No email sending is wired up yet (Section 9 - Email Sending is queued) so there's no real token delivery in this environment.
Needs a real reset token from the (not-yet-wired) email flow — will 400 RESET_FAILED without one.
Called by the Next.js auth adapter after a provider sign-in. If issueTokens=true, behaves like Login (sets refresh cookie, returns tokens).

item.description: No auth required. Run Signup then Login first — everything downstream needs access_token.

request.description: Returns { user: SafeUser }. Also see GET /me and GET /users/me (User Profile folder) which return the same shape via a different module.

Revokes the current refresh session and clears the cookie. Always returns 204, even if the token was already invalid. Not behind RequireAuth (so an expired-access-token user can still log out). Aliased as POST /auth/sign-out.
Revokes every refresh session for the user. Aliased as POST /auth/sign-out-all.
Expects multipart/form-data with an image file field — set the body manually in Postman (form-data, key 'avatar', type File).

item.name: 28 - Capture / Public Endpoints

request.description: Requires header X-API-Key with a key created above (scope capture:leads). This is the one capture-side endpoint the r11 audit confirmed WORKS end-to-end. Unrecognized top-level fields (anything beyond first_name/last_name/email/phone/company_name/title) are stored in custom_fields automatically — see utm_source/utm_campaign here. As of the latest source pull, both capture_source and the lead's plain source field are tagged 'website' (previously capture_source was 'web_form' and source was left null). The /pub group also now carries its own permissive CORS (AllowOrigins: '*') separate from the rest of the API — irrelevant to Postman itself, but relevant if you're testing this from a browser-based embed.

Requires header X-API-Key with a key that has the capture:visitors scope. Manual Segment-style identify — traits.email/name/company map to a lead. This is NOT IP→company enrichment (no IPinfo, no background worker) — that's a queued, separate build item.

⚠️ NO signature verification yet (Fix Pass B item 8, WEBHOOK_EMAIL_SECRET pending) — do not expose this route to the public internet until that lands. Org is resolved from the 'to' address, which must first be registered via Capture / Email below. Accepts JSON or multipart/form-data (SendGrid-style).

⚠️ Currently accepts ANY non-empty hub.verify_token (Fix Pass B item 9, real FACEBOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN comparison pending) and returns hub.challenge as plain text. Also has no X-Hub-Signature-256 check on the POST path below.

⚠️ No X-Hub-Signature-256 verification yet (Fix Pass B item 9). Also, per the r11 doc, this is a webhook SKELETON, not a real Graph API integration — it maps flat payload fields directly, which is not the shape a real Facebook Lead Ads webhook actually sends (no leadgen_id→Graph API fetch). Route is registered with .All() so technically accepts any HTTP method, but only GET (challenge) and POST (payload) have real logic.
